plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DESeq2 DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human lung bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated, 6 control; 12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol) quantified with salmon, and batch B1/B2 is perfectly confounded with condition (all controls in B1, all treated in B2). Because the design matrix condition ~ batch is not full rank, no batch term, ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, or SVA-style correction can be fit or applied without also removing the condition signal — this is a hard constraint from the knowledge-base rule R-0005, not a modeling nicety. The plan therefore: (1) QCs the sample structure with a blind VST/PCA/distance heatmap so any batch-vs-condition separation is visualized and reported as a caveat rather than corrected away; (2) filters low-count genes minimally; (3) runs DESeq2 Wald test with an explicit reference level (condition ~ condition, Control as reference) and apeglm shrinkage as the primary DE call, plus edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same design as a second method for a robustness/overlap check (per R-0042); (4) applies BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 and reports the count of significant genes; (5) runs fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary) human gene sets, which are present in the reference store, since gene-level results are expected to be confounded and gene set-level results are somewhat more robust to sample-level batch noise but still not deconfoundable; (6) produces a report that states plainly, for every result, that condition and batch are indistinguishable in this design, so 'differential expression' findings are candidates that could equally be a batch/processing artifact, and that only a follow-up experiment with a non-confounded design (or existing rebalanced batches) can separate the two explanations. No causal claim about the treatment is licensed by this dataset alone.
